title: The exact finite-cutoff stationary diagonal Gaussian minimizer converges to the profiled coefficient

finite_cutoff_minimizer.fixed_variance_problem: For cutoff modes omega_k and prescribed point variance V, strict convexity minimizes sum_k omega_k(s_k+s_k^(-1)-2)/4 subject to V=sum_k s_k/(2omega_k). The unique profile is s_(N,k)=omega_k/sqrt(omega_k^2+kappa).
finite_cutoff_minimizer.reduced_data: Write A_N(kappa)=(1/2)sum_k(omega_k^2+kappa)^(-1/2), D_N(kappa)=C_N-A_N(kappa), and F_N^*(A_N(kappa)) for the minimized free cost. On the active-mean branch y_N=3D_N-m^2/(4g).
finite_cutoff_minimizer.exact_euler_equation: For all sufficiently large N the active branch has two critical parameters kappa_(g,N)^-<kappa_(g,N)^+ satisfying kappa+3m^2=24gD_N(kappa). The smaller is the finite-mass barrier near the vacuum endpoint; the larger is the minimizing profile.
finite_cutoff_minimizer.uniqueness: D_N is strictly increasing and strictly concave with D_N(0)=0, so f_N(kappa)=kappa+3m^2-24gD_N(kappa) is strictly convex. For large N its minimum is negative, giving exactly two roots. The reduced derivative makes the smaller root a local maximum and the larger root the unique active local minimum; K1567's strict coefficient gain makes the larger root the global stationary-diagonal minimizer over the vacuum and inactive branches.
finite_cutoff_minimizer.coefficient_limit: Riemann-sum convergence and the uniqueness of K1567's positive continuum solution imply kappa_(g,N)^+/N^2 tends to kappa_g while kappa_(g,N)^-/N^2 tends to zero. The minimizing s_(N,k) approaches |k|/sqrt(|k|^2+kappa_gN^2) at rescaled frequencies, and the exact stationary diagonal Gaussian minimum divided by N^4 tends to h_g^prof.
finite_cutoff_minimizer.advance: K1567's explicit recovery sequence is therefore asymptotically exact for the complete stationary translation-invariant diagonal Gaussian class, not merely one upper trial.
finite_cutoff_minimizer.scope_guard: This is a matching coefficient theorem only inside the stationary diagonal Gaussian class. It is not an unrestricted non-Gaussian lower bound, an O(1) expansion, a true ground-state profile, ground-energy ratio convergence or a source-owned GU Hamiltonian.
